Reminder

# Page 5^page=5
Covariant derivatives Covariant derivatives The covariant derivatives are de˝ned by Ai,k = ∂Ai ∂xk + Aj ∂ej ∂xk · ei, Ai ,k = ∂Ai ∂xk + Aj ∂ej ∂xk 2 28

# Page 6^page=6
Christoffel Symbol Christo˙el Symbol The covariant derivatives are de˝ned by Ai,k = ∂Ai ∂xk + Aj ∂ej ∂xk · ei, Ai ,k = ∂Ai ∂xk + Aj ∂ej ∂xk · e i. We then de˝ne Γ i jk = e i · ∂ej ∂xk and Γ j ik = −ei · ∂ej ∂xk , called Christo˙el symbols of the second kind . 3 28

# Page 7^page=7
Covariant differentiation in terms of Christoffel symbols Covariant di˙erentiation in terms of Christo˙el symbols If we re-write the covariant derivatives using Christo˙el symbols, we get Ai,k = ∂Ai ∂xk − Γ j ikAj, Ai ,k = ∂Ai ∂xk + Γi jkAj, where Γi jk = e i · ∂ej ∂xk and Γ j ik = −ei · ∂ej ∂xk . 4 28

# Page 8^page=8
Back to a fixed basis Back to a ˝xed basis Once more, covariant derivatives are de˝ned by Ai,k = ∂Ai ∂xk − Γ j ikAj, Ai ,k = ∂Ai ∂xk + Γi jkAj. We have seen that, if the basis is ˝xed , then the Christo˙el symbols vanish: Γ i jk = e i · ∂ej ∂xk = 0. Then the covariant derivatives Ai,k and Ai ,k reduce simply to ∂Ai,k = Ai ∂xk and ∂A i ,k = Ai ∂xk . 5 28

# Page 9^page=9
Christoffel symbols as expansion coefficients Christo˙el symbols as expansion coe˚cients Notice that Γ i jk = e i · ∂ej ∂xk =⇒ ∂ej ∂xk = Γ i jkei, thus Γi jk are the expansion coe˚cients of the vector ∂ej ∂xk with respect to the basis e1, e2, e3. That is, if we write ∂ej ∂xk = A 1e1 + A2e2 + A3e3, then the coe˚cients A1, A2, A3 are given by Ai = Γ i jk. 6 28

# Page 10^page=10
Christoffel symbols as expansion coeffi- cients - Part 2 Christo˙el symbols as expansion coe˚cients We can also expand the vector ∂ej ∂xk with respect to the dual basis e1, e2, e3. We denote the coe˚cients of this expansion by Γijk. That is ∂ej ∂xk = Γijke i =⇒ Γijk = ei · ∂ej ∂xk . These new symbols are called the Christo˙el symbols of the ˝rst kind . 7 28

# Page 11^page=11
Definitions: Two types of Christoffel Symbol De˝nitions. Christo˙el symbols of second kind : Γi jk = e i · ∂ej ∂xk . Christo˙el symbols of ˝rst kind : Γijk = ei · ∂ej ∂xk . 8 28

# Page 12^page=12
Christoffel symbols and metric tensors Christo˙el symbols and metric tensors Christo˙el symbols of the ˝rst and second kind are related via the metric tensor: Γijk = giℓΓ ℓ jk, Γ i jk = giℓΓℓkj, where the Christo˙el symbols are Γ i jk = e i · ∂ej ∂xk and Γijk = ei · ∂ej ∂xk , and the metric tensor is giℓ = ei · eℓ and giℓ = e i · e ℓ. 9 28

# Page 13^page=13
Summary: Christoffel Symbols and the Metric Tensor Summary: Christo˙el Symbols and the Metric Tensor Christo˙el symbols of second kind Γi jk = e i · ∂ej ∂xk . Christo˙el symbols of ˝rst kind Γijk = ei · ∂ej ∂xk . Christo˙el symbols of the ˝rst and second kind are related via the metric tensor Γijk = giℓΓ ℓ jk, Γ i jk = giℓΓℓkj. 10 28

# Page 14^page=14
Christoffel Symbols formula

# Page 15^page=15
Generalised coordinate system - Christof- fel symbol formula Generalised coordinate system - Christo˙el symbol formula Because Γijk is symmetric in j, k, we can write Γijk = 1 2 (Γijk + Γikj). Using the de˝nition Γijk = ei · ∂ej ∂xk , we get 1 2 (Γijk + Γikj) = 1 2 ( ei · ∂ej ∂xk + ei · ∂ek ∂xj ) . 11 28

# Page 16^page=16
Generalised coordinate system - Christof- fel symbol formula -Part 2 Generalised coordinate system - Christo˙el symbol formula We then obtain Γijk = 1 2 ( ei · ∂ej ∂xk + ei · ∂ek ∂xj ) = 1 2 ( ∂ ∂xk (ei · ej) + ∂ ∂xj (ei · ek) − ej · ∂ei ∂xk − ek · ∂ei ∂xj ) = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ej · ∂ek ∂xi − ek · ∂ej ∂xi ) = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂ ∂xi (ej · ek) ) , = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) . 12 28

# Page 17^page=17
Summary - Christoffel symbol formula Summary - Christo˙el symbol formula Christo˙el symbol of the ˝rst kind is related to the metric tensor of the underlying generalised coodinate system via Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) . 13 28

# Page 18^page=18
Generalised coordinate system - Christof- fel symbol formula - Second kind Generalised coordinate system - Christo˙el symbol formula Since the Christo˙el symbol of the ˝rst kind is given by Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) , and we have the relation Γ i jk = giℓΓℓkj, we can derive a formula for Christo˙el symbols of the second kind: Γ i jk = 1 2 giℓ ( ∂gℓj ∂xk + ∂gℓk ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xℓ ) . 14 28

# Page 19^page=19
Example Example Suppose a coordinate system (x1, x2, x3) = (ρ, ϕ, θ) has metric tensors given by g11 = 1, g22 = r2, g33 = sin ϕ sin θ, and the other components of the metric tensor are trivial. Using Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) ˝nd all Christo˙el symbols of the ˝rst and second kind 15 28

# Page 20^page=20
Example - Part 2 Example In the coordinate system (x1, x2, x3) = (ρ, ϕ, θ), we have g11 = 1, g22 = r2, g33 = sin ϕ sin θ, and we know that the Christo˙el symbols of ˝rst kind are given by Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) . The ˝rst step is then to determine which partial derivatives ∂gij ∂xk are non-zero. Note that all gij are constant, except for g22 = r2 and g33 = sin ϕ sin θ. Thus ∂gij ∂xk = 0, unless (i, j, k) = (2, 2, 1), (3, 3, 2), (3, 3, 3). 16 28

# Page 21^page=21
Example - Part 3 Example Since ∂gij ∂xk = 0, unless (i, j, k) = (2, 2, 1), (3, 3, 2), (3, 3, 3), and Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) , the only possibly non-zero Christo˙el symbols are the ones having 2, 2, 1, or 3, 3, 2, or 3, 3, 2 as indices (in some order). 17 28

# Page 22^page=22
Example - Part 4 Example Since (x1, x2, x3) = (ρ, ϕ, θ) and g22 = r2, g33 = sin ϕ sin θ, we obtain ∂g22 ∂x1 = ∂r2 ∂r = 2r ∂g33 ∂x2 = ∂(sin ϕ sin θ) ∂ϕ = cos ϕ sin θ, ∂g33 ∂x3 = ∂(sin ϕ sin θ) ∂θ = sin ϕ cos θ. 18 28

# Page 23^page=23
Example - Part 5 Example Let us combine everything. We found The only posisbly non-zero Christo˙el symvbols are Γ122, Γ212, Γ221, Γ233, Γ323, Γ332, Γ333. The non-zero partial derivatives are ∂g22 ∂x1 = 2r, ∂g33 ∂x2 = cos ϕ sin θ, ∂g33 ∂x3 sin ϕ cos θ. The Christo˙el symbols of ˝rst kind are given by Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) . 19 28

# Page 24^page=24
Example - Part 6 Example Thus Γ122 = 1 2 ( ∂g12 ∂x2 + ∂g12 ∂x2 − ∂g22 ∂x1 ) = − 1 2 ∂g22 ∂x1 = − 1 2 2r = −r. Γ212 = 1 2 ( ∂g21 ∂x2 + ∂g22 ∂x1 − ∂g12 ∂x2 ) = 1 2 ∂g22 ∂x1 = 1 2 2r = r. Since the Chisto˙el symbols are symmetric in their last two indices, we also conclude Γ221 = Γ212 = r. 20 28

# Page 25^page=25
Example - Part 7 Example Moreover Γ233 = 1 2 ( ∂g23 ∂x3 + ∂g23 ∂x3 − ∂g33 ∂x2 ) = − 1 2 ∂g33 ∂x2 = − 1 2 (cos ϕ sin θ). Γ323 = Γ332 = 1 2 ( ∂g32 ∂x3 + ∂g33 ∂x3 − ∂g23 ∂x3 ) = 1 2 ∂g33 ∂x3 = 1 2 (cos ϕ sin θ), Γ333 = 1 2 ( ∂g33 ∂x3 + ∂g33 ∂x3 − ∂g33 ∂x3 ) = 1 2 ∂g33 ∂x3 = 1 2 (sin ϕ cos θ). 21 28

# Page 26^page=26
Example - Part 8 Example Thus, the Christo˙el symbols of ˝rst kind are given by Γ122 = −r, Γ221 = Γ212 = r, Γ233 = − 1 2 (cos ϕ sin θ) Γ323 = Γ332 = 1 2 (cos ϕ sin θ), Γ333 = 1 2 (sin ϕ cos θ), and Γijk = 0, for all other values of i, j, k. 22 28

# Page 27^page=27
Example - Part 9 Example To ˝nd the Christo˙el symbols of second kind , we use the formula Γ i jk = giℓΓℓkj and gii = 1/gii. We have Γ 1 22 = g1ℓΓℓ22 = g11Γ122 + g12Γ222 + g13Γ322 = g11Γ122 = 1 g11 Γ122 = 1 1 · (−r) = −r. Similarly, Γ2 21 = Γ 2 12 = g2ℓΓℓ21 = g22Γ221 = 1 r2 · r = 1 r . 23 28

# Page 28^page=28
Example - Last step Example Following the same steps for the other Christo˙el symbols of second kind , we ˝nd Γ1 22 = −r, Γ2 21 = Γ 2 12 = 1 r , Γ2 33 = − cos ϕ sin θ 2r2 , Γ3 23 = Γ 3 32 = 1 2 tan ϕ , Γ3 33 = 1 2 tan θ , and Γi jk = 0, for all other values of i, j, k. 24 28

# Page 29^page=29
Task Your turn! In Exercise 5.5, you showed that, in spherical coordinates (x1, x2, x3) = (r, ϕ, θ), the metric tensors are g11 = 1, g22 = r2, g33 = r2 sin 2 ϕ, and the other components of the metric tensor are trivial. Using Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gij ∂xk + ∂gik ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xi ) ˝nd all Christo˙el symbols of the ˝rst and second kind 25 28

Covariant differentiation of tensors

# Page 31^page=31
Recap of vectors Recap of vectors Recall that the covariant derivatives of a vector can be written in terms of the Christo˙el symbol of the second kind: Ai,k = ∂Ai ∂xk − Γ j ikAj, Ai ,k = ∂Ai ∂xk + Γi jkAj. 26 28

# Page 32^page=32
Second rank tensors Second rank tensors Likewise, we have formulae for the covariant derivative of components of second-rank tensors: Tik,ℓ = ∂Tik ∂xℓ − Γm iℓTmk − Γm kℓTim T ik ,ℓ = ∂T ik ∂xℓ + Γi mℓT mk + Γk mℓT im T i .k,ℓ = ∂T i .k ∂xℓ + Γi mℓT m .k − Γ m kℓT i .m. These quantities Tik,ℓ, T ik ,ℓ, T i .k,ℓ transform under the appropriate tensor transformation law respectively (Exercise). 27 28
